purpose: Compare exact shipped GLB bytes across direct fetch+parse and Three FileLoader using production shared-cache/clone/disposal ownership, retaining the exact Response delivered to each fetch-backed consumer.
cases: For each asset, concurrent shared-cache reads whose single factory fetches and parseAsyncs the exact bytes; body assets clone twice with production cloneSkinnedBodyScene.
For each asset, hash reference bytes then concurrent shared-cache reads whose single factory uses GLTFLoader.loadAsync; body assets clone twice with production cloneSkinnedBodyScene.

Retain exact GLB Response objects returned by fetch (including FileLoader's fetch), reference ArrayBuffers, parsed templates, resolved cache values and clone references until report formation; release actor clone resources before cached template resources.
strictGate: Any failed, canceled, or pending GLB request; HTTP error; runtime exception; or console error fails. No retry, filtering, or cancellation waiver.
instrumentation: Passive fetch start/response and arrayBuffer completion with bodyUsed/byte counts; retain exact Response without cloning or reading stream in observer.
Passive XHR open/send/readyState/progress/load/loadend/abort/error/timeout plus direct abort-call stack; supplemental because prior CDP evidence showed FileLoader uses fetch here.
AbortController.abort calls and CDP request initiator, response/data/terminal lifecycle.
limitations: Exercises the production shared cache and clone helper, but not full loadBody appearance/renderer lifecycle.
Strong references test persistence under retained ownership; they do not prove garbage collection caused a cancellation.
No avatar pixels, mobile performance, or gameplay acceptance are measured.
